2608.07705.title: Protecting patient privacy in clinical foundation models: Technical and legal perspectives
2608.07705.paper_summary: Clinical foundation models trained on large-scale patient data are increasingly used for decision support, screening, and public health. As deployment expands, privacy risk increasingly arises from model-mediated leakage, yet its prevalence and severity remain poorly quantified. Models can disclose sensitive training artifacts, enabling patient re-identification in ways not captured by data-handling controls alone. Existing frameworks, including HIPAA and GDPR, offer limited guidance for such indirect threats. We propose a practical framework for assessing privacy risk in clinical foundation models and illustrate realistic leakage scenarios across deployment settings, map them to legal regimes, and outline complementary technical and legal mitigations. Our analysis provides a context-aware risk assessment grounded in realistic usage to preserve the value of medical foundation models while rigorously safeguarding patient privacy.
2608.07705.paper_summary_zh: 臨床基礎模型在大型患者數據上訓練，越來越多地用於決策支持、篩查和公共衛生。隨著部署的擴展，隱私風險越來越多地來自模型中介的洩漏，但其普遍性和嚴重性仍然缺乏量化。模型可能會披露敏感的訓練產物，使患者重新識別的方式無法僅通過數據處理控制來捕捉。現有的框架，包括HIPAA和GDPR，對於這種間接威脅提供的指導有限。我們提出了一個實用的框架，用於評估臨床基礎模型中的隱私風險，並展示了在不同部署環境中的現實洩漏場景，將其映射到法律體系中，並概述補充的技術和法律緩解措施。我們的分析提供了一種基於現實使用的上下文感知風險評估，以保護醫療基礎模型的價值，同時嚴格保護患者隱私。
